info.title: RACS REST API
info.description: A RestAPI for configuring and controlling GEV cameras using Rust and Aravis.

get.description: Returns a list of devices that are connected to the network

200.description: Discovered devices in network. The id is used for connecting to devices

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

get.description: Returns the devices this server is currently connected to. Unlike `GET /devices` this runs no network discovery, so it answers immediately and is cheap enough to poll. A device that is busy streaming is still listed. Each entry carries its `access` state (as `GET /devices/{id}/access` reports it to this client).

200.description: Connected devices

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

get.description:
The device's access mode, its owner (the session holding the lease), its member sessions, what holds its camera (`live` or `burst`, and who started it), its live viewers, and `you`: this client's role (`owner`, `writer`, `reader` or `meta`).

| mode | owner | other sessions | anonymous |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shared` (default) | – | read + write | read + write |
| `ro-shared` | read + write | read | meta |
| `exclusive` | read + write | meta | meta |

Meta routes are the GenICam XML and categories, `stream/error` and this one. Doesn't connect the device.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id

200.description: The device's access state

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

put.description:
Takes or changes the device's lease (`ro-shared`, `exclusive`), or gives it up (`shared`), connecting the device if needed. Needs a session; the lease ends when its owner releases it, when the owner's session ends, on a force, or when the device closes, and the mode returns to `shared`.

Taking a lease another session owns is refused with `423` unless `force`. Going `exclusive` while other sessions are members of the device or another client's live stream or burst holds it is refused with `409` unless `force`, which evicts them: they leave the device, their live sockets close with `4003` (`access revoked`), their running bursts are cancelled (error `access revoked`), and each evicted session gets `access_revoked` on its events socket.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id

200.description: The device's access state after the change

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

409.description: `device_in_use`: `exclusive` while other sessions are members or another client's stream or burst holds the device

500.description: The device could not be connected

delete.description: Gives up the device's lease (its owner), or breaks it (anyone, with `force`; the owner gets `access_revoked`). The mode returns to `shared`. Nothing to do on a device without a lease. Needs a session.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Break another session's lease

200.description: The device's access state after the release

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

put.description:
Connects to a device by id. If the ip is specified, it will be used to connect to the device, choose an id which will be assigned to this device. If the ip is not specified, the device will be discovered using the GV interface. If the device is already connected, this will do nothing. With a session, the session becomes a member of the device, which keeps it connected until the session leaves (`PUT /devices/{id}/disconnect`) or ends.

With `mode` (`shared`, `ro-shared` or `exclusive`; needs a session) the connect takes the device's lease in one atomic step, with the same rules as `PUT /devices/{id}/access` without `force`. Without `mode` the client joins in the device's current mode. Answers the device's access state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: IP address of device

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Take the lease in this mode

200.description: Connected; the device's access state

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

409.description: `device_in_use`: `exclusive` while other clients use the device

put.description:
Disconnects a device by id. If the device is not connected, this will do nothing.

Several clients may use a device. With a session, this *leaves* the device: the camera closes only when no other session is a member and no live stream or burst job holds it. Without a session, it closes the device unless a session is a member of it or holds it with a stream or burst. `?force=true` closes it for everyone and needs write permission (`403`/`423` otherwise). `closed` in the answer says whether the device is closed now, `members` how many sessions still use it.

When the device closes, a live stream on it is stopped and its socket closed with `1001` (`device disconnected`); a running burst job is cancelled and keeps its record (status `cancelled`, error `device disconnected`, the images taken so far). Requests for the device that arrive meanwhile wait for the disconnect, then connect it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Close the device for everyone

200.description: Left or disconnected the device

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: `force` on a `ro-shared` device by a reader

423.description: `device_locked`: `force` on a device another session's lease locks

get.description: Returns the GenICam categories of a device by id. The categories are returned as a list of GenICamNodeCategory structs. Each struct contains the category name and a list of feature nodes. The feature nodes are returned as a list of GenICamNode structs. Each struct contains the node name, node type, and node value. The node value is returned as a string. Use the query parameter value to set the value of the feature. The value must be a string. The value can be retrieved using get devices/{id}/gc/feature/{feature_name} and set using put devices/{id}/gc/feature/{feature_name}?value={value}

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

200.description: GenICam categories with feature node info

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

post.description: Executes a GenICam Command feature (node_type `Command` in /devices/{id}/gc/categories), such as TriggerSoftware, UserSetLoad or UserSetSave. Not idempotent: each request executes the command once. Works during a live stream like the feature routes; AcquisitionStart/AcquisitionStop are refused then.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

parameters.name: command_name
parameters.description: Name of the command feature

200.description: Command executed

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: Unknown feature, not a command, or the device refused it

get.description: Returns the GenICam feature value of a device by id. The feature name must match with nodes of /devices/{id}/gc/categories. The value is returned as a string.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

parameters.name: feature_name
parameters.description: Name of the feature

200.description: Get GenICam feature value as string

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

put.description: Sets the GenICam feature value of a device by id. The feature name must match with nodes of /devices/{id}/gc/categories. The value must be a string: an integer for Integer and Enum features (an Enum also takes its symbolic entry name), a number for Float, `true`/`false` (or `1`/`0`) for Boolean. Commands have no value; execute them with POST /devices/{id}/gc/command/{name}. The value can be retrieved using get devices/{id}/gc/feature/{feature_name} and set using put devices/{id}/gc/feature/{feature_name}?value={value}. While a live stream runs on the device, reads and writes are carried out inside the stream (which restarts acquisition if the change alters the payload) instead of failing as busy; PixelFormat and the stream destination (GevSCDA, GevSCPHostPort) are refused then. During a burst job they still fail as busy. GevSCPSPacketSize must be a multiple of its increment within its bounds and not above the link MTU (see GET /devices/{id}/stream/packet-size); it applies to every following grab, stream and burst.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

parameters.name: feature_name
parameters.description: Name of the feature

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value as string

200.description: Value has been set

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

post.description: Returns the live state of several GenICam features in one request, in the order asked: the value (formatted as by GET /devices/{id}/gc/feature/{feature_name}), whether the feature is currently available and locked, and for numeric features their evaluated min/max/increment, unit and representation. For an Enum, `available_entries` lists the integer values of the entries the device currently offers. A problem with one feature (unknown name, failed read) is reported in that entry's `error`, not as a failed request. Works during a live stream like the single-feature routes. 400 for an empty list or more than 256 names.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

200.description: One state per requested name, in request order

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: The device could not be reached, or is busy with a burst job

post.description:
Starts a background job that grabs `count` frames from the device and keeps them in memory. The response is returned before the capture starts, so this never blocks for the duration of the burst; poll `GET /devices/{id}/grab/jobs/{job_id}` for progress and fetch the frames from the `images` routes.

The camera is held exclusively for the whole run, exactly like a live stream — every other request for that device fails while the job is capturing. A device that is *already* busy is not detected here, because the camera is only taken once the background task starts: such a job is created normally and then transitions straight to `failed`, so check the status rather than assuming a `202` means the capture began.

`format` is `raw`, `jpeg` or `zstd`. `pixel_depth` is `mono8` (default) or `mono16`; the latter asks the camera for the deepest unpacked mono format it supports (Mono16, 14, 12, then 10; Coord3D_C16 on a 3D camera in Linescan3D). Raw images are width*height bytes in 8-bit and width*height little-endian u16s above that; the job status reports `width`, `height`, `pixel_format` and `bit_depth` once the first frame is in. JPEG images always hold the top 8 significant bits. `zstd` images are the raw ones losslessly compressed, decoded as described for the live stream (`GET /devices/{id}/stream/live`); frames are compressed while the capture goes on, and the job completes once every one is stored. `quality` (1-100, default 80) applies to `jpeg` only and is clamped rather than rejected. `on_failure` is `abort` (default: the first frame that cannot be grabbed fails the job) or `skip` (record the failure at that index and carry on, up to `max_failures`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device to grab from

202.description: Job accepted; the capture runs in the background

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: The device could not be connected

get.description: Reports a burst job's progress. `captured_count` and `failed_count` advance while the job runs; `expires_at` is null until the job reaches `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`, after which the job and its images are dropped automatically at that time unless deleted sooner. `error` is set only for a failed job.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device the job belongs to

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job id returned when the job was started

200.description: Current job state

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

404.description: No such job for this device

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

delete.description: Cancels a running job or discards a finished one — the job and its images are gone either way. A job that is still capturing stops within a fraction of a second and releases the camera; its partial images are discarded with it, so fetch anything worth keeping first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device the job belongs to

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job id returned when the job was started

204.description: The job was cancelled and/or removed

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

404.description: No such job for this device

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

get.description: Lists the frames a burst job has attempted so far, in capture order — safe to poll while the job is still running, since the array simply grows. Each entry is either `{"status":"ok","index","size_bytes"}` or `{"status":"failed","index","error"}`; a failed entry only appears for a job started with `on_failure=skip`. Fetch the bytes of an entry from `/devices/{id}/grab/jobs/{job_id}/images/{index}`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device the job belongs to

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job id returned when the job was started

200.description: Metadata for every index captured so far

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

404.description: No such job for this device

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

get.description:
Returns one captured frame, in the `format` the job was started with. The content type is `application/octet-stream` for `raw`, `jpeg` and `zstd` alike, matching the single-frame endpoints. A `zstd` frame decodes as described for the live stream (`GET /devices/{id}/stream/live`), with the job's `width`, `height` and `bit_depth`.

`404` covers both an index the job has not reached yet and one past the end of the burst; `410` means that index was attempted and failed, with the reason as the body.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device the job belongs to

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job id returned when the job was started

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Zero-based index into the burst

200.description: The captured frame

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

404.description: No such job, or that index has not been captured

410.description: That index was attempted and failed

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

get.description: Returns why the last live stream on this device ended, whether one is running right now, and how many sockets watch it (`viewers`). A closed WebSocket carries its reason away with it, so this is how a client finds out after the fact. `last_error` and `timestamp` are null for a device whose streams have never failed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device to report on

200.description: Last live-stream error and current stream state

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

get.description: Grabs a frame from the device and encodes it as a jpeg. The quality can be set using the query parameter quality. The default quality is 80. By default the pixel format is set to MONO8

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device to grab the frame from

200.description: Successfully started streaming the jpeg frame

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

get.description: Grabs a raw frame from the device.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device to grab the frame from

200.description: Successfully started streaming the raw frame

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

get.description:
Opens a WebSocket that streams frames continuously until the client disconnects. This is not an ordinary HTTP request: the response is a `101 Switching Protocols` upgrade, and clients must use a WebSocket implementation rather than a REST call.

The server sends one text message first, describing the stream:
`{"width":1280,"height":1024,"format":"jpeg","pixel_format":"Mono8","bit_depth":8,"packet_size":1500}`. Raw consumers need it, because the binary messages carry no dimensions. `packet_size` is the GevSCPSPacketSize the stream runs with. With `bit_depth` above 8, raw images are width*height little-endian u16s in the range `0..2^bit_depth`; JPEG images always hold the top 8 significant bits.

`zstd` images are the raw pixels, losslessly compressed (about half the size of raw on a camera image, at a few ms of server CPU per frame). Each is one zstd frame with its content size in the header. Decompressed, it holds a residual per pixel, row by row: the pixel minus the one above it (minus 0 in the first row), wrapping at the pixel width. At 8 bit that is width*height bytes. Above 8 bit each residual `d` (taken as i16) is zigzagged to `z = (d << 1) ^ (d >> 15)`, and the data is every low byte of `z` followed by every high byte. To decode, un-zigzag (`d = (z >> 1) ^ -(z & 1)`) and add the decoded pixel above, wrapping at 8 or 16 bits: a cumulative sum down each column.

Every message after that is binary: `[4 bytes frame_number (u32 LE)][4 bytes frames_dropped (u32 LE)][image data]`. Frame numbers start at 0 and count messages actually sent to this socket; the dropped counter is cumulative for the socket and never resets, covering incomplete frames, frames skipped by its fps limit, and frames dropped because this client could not keep up.

The text message is repeated whenever the geometry or the packet size changes mid-stream (a Width or GevSCPSPacketSize written while streaming, say): it describes every binary message after it, until the next one. Frame numbers and the dropped counter carry on across it.

Several clients can watch a device at once. The first socket starts the capture, later ones join it, and each has its own `format`, `quality`, `fps`, frame numbers and dropped counter; a slow client drops frames without slowing the others down. `pixel_depth` is decided by whoever started the capture: a socket asking for another depth gets the running one, announced in `bit_depth`. The capture stops when its last socket closes. The camera is held while it runs, so frame grabs and burst jobs for that device fail meanwhile. GenICam feature reads, writes and commands are carried out inside the running stream instead, between frames. Features the camera locks during acquisition (`pIsLocked` on `TLParamsLocked`, e.g. ExposureTime, AcquisitionFrameRate, Width) are written with acquisition paused for a moment, since a camera may otherwise store them but keep using the old value; the request answers once acquisition runs again. GevSCPSPacketSize and `POST /devices/{id}/stream/packet-size/auto` take the same pause, and the stream reopens its channel with the new size. A change that alters the payload size or pixel format also restarts acquisition, and so does a write the device refuses while acquiring. PixelFormat (set from `pixel_depth`), the stream destination (GevSCDA, GevSCPHostPort) and AcquisitionStart/Stop are refused while streaming. Every socket is closed on any acquisition error; ask `GET /devices/{id}/stream/error` for the reason. When the device is disconnected (`PUT /devices/{id}/disconnect`), the capture stops and every socket is closed with `1001` (going away) and the reason `device disconnected`.

A viewer that carries a session (`?session=`) is one of its heartbeats: the server pings it every `heartbeat_interval_s` and every pong or message keeps the session alive. When the session ends its socket is closed with `4001` (`session expired`); the capture runs on for the other sockets.

Starting a capture needs write permission on the device, joining a running one read permission. A refused request is answered with its status before the upgrade (browsers only see a failed connection, so the reason is also recorded for `GET /devices/{id}/stream/error`). When another session takes the device `exclusive` with `force`, the sockets of every other client are closed with `4003` (`access revoked`); the capture keeps running for that session's own sockets, if it has any.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device to stream from

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `jpeg` (default), `raw` (width*height pixels, 1 or 2 bytes each per `bit_depth`) or `zstd` (the raw pixels, losslessly compressed as described above)

parameters.name: pixel_depth
parameters.description: `mono8` (default) or `mono16`: the deepest unpacked mono format the camera accepts (Mono16, 14, 12, then 10; Coord3D_C16 on a 3D camera in Linescan3D)

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: JPEG quality 1-100, default 80. Ignored for raw and zstd

parameters.name: fps
parameters.description: Target frame rate. Omit to send every frame the camera delivers

101.description: WebSocket upgrade accepted; frames follow on the socket

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: The device could not be connected or the upgrade failed

get.description: Returns the stream packet size (GevSCPSPacketSize: bytes per GVSP packet, IP and UDP headers included), the values it may take, and the MTU of the local interface the camera is reached over. Every grab, live stream and burst uses the camera's packet size as it is; change it with `PUT /devices/{id}/gc/feature/GevSCPSPacketSize?value=` or let `POST /devices/{id}/stream/packet-size/auto` find the largest that works. Packets larger than the link MTU never arrive, so jumbo frames (e.g. 7960) need an interface MTU of 9000. Answered during a live stream too; busy during a burst.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device

200.description: Packet size, its bounds and the link

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: The device could not be reached

post.description: Finds the largest stream packet size that reaches this host and sets it, the way Aravis does: the camera fires GigE Vision test packets with "don't fragment" set, and a binary search between the packet size bounds (capped at the link MTU) keeps the largest that arrives. Takes up to about a second. During a live stream, acquisition pauses for it and the stream carries on with the new size. A camera that answers no test packet keeps its packet size (`test_packets: false`). Busy during a burst. On connect the server already checks the camera's packet size this way and only replaces it when it doesn't get through.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the device

200.description: The packet size now set

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

403.description: `read_only`: the device is `ro-shared` and this session isn't its owner

423.description: `device_locked`: the device is `exclusive` for another session (or `ro-shared` and this client anonymous)

500.description: The device could not be reached or is busy

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Device id, can be found using get devices

200.description: Xml as string

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

get.description:
A WebSocket of what happens on the server; requires a session (`?session=<session_id>`, since a browser can't set headers on a WebSocket). It is the session's heartbeat too: the server pings every `heartbeat_interval_s`, and every pong or message keeps the session alive.

Every message is JSON text with a global `seq`, an RFC 3339 `time` and a `type`:
- `hello` first: `session` (`client_id`, `timeout_s`) and `devices`, the state of every connected device. Its `seq` is the last event the snapshot includes.
- `device_state`: a device's complete state (`device`, `connected`, `access` = `{mode, owner, members}`, `stream` = `{viewers, pixel_format, bit_depth}` or null, `burst` = `{job_id, client_id}` or null), with `cause` (`connected`, `disconnected`, `access`, `stream`, `burst`), `reason` (for a disconnect: `request`, `idle`, `forced`, `error`) and `by`.
- `feature_changed` (`device`, `feature`, `by`): no value, since a write changes dependent features too; read again what you show. Includes writes made during a live stream and the GevSCPSPacketSize set by `POST /devices/{id}/stream/packet-size/auto`.
- `command_executed` (`device`, `command`, `by`).
- `session_ended` (`client_id`, `reason`: `expired` or `closed`).
- `resync`: this socket fell behind and lost events; read the state again.

`by` is `{client_id, name}`, or null for anonymous clients and the server itself. Clients use `seq` only to notice gaps. When the session ends the socket is closed with `4001` (`session expired`).

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: The secret session id

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

get.description: The live sessions, oldest first, as other clients see them: never with a `session_id`.

200.description: Live sessions

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

post.description:
Starts a client session. Clients without one keep working as before (anonymously); a session gives a client an identity other clients see (`client_id`, `name`), makes it a member of the devices it uses, and lets it subscribe to `GET /events`.

Send `session_id` with every request, as the header `X-Racs-Session` or the query parameter `?session=` (WebSockets need the query parameter). It is a secret; `client_id` is public. Each request carrying it is a heartbeat, and so is `POST /sessions/{session_id}/heartbeat` and every pong or message on a WebSocket carrying it. A session without a heartbeat for `timeout_s` ends; send one every `heartbeat_interval_s`. The body is optional: `timeout_s` defaults to the server's `--session-timeout` and is clamped to 5..=600.

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

delete.description: Ends a session now, as an expiry would: it leaves every device (which then closes after the idle timeout if nobody else uses it), its WebSockets are closed with `4001`, and `session_ended` is sent. Its burst jobs run to completion. `204` for an unknown session too.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The secret session id

401.description: The session is unknown or has expired (`session_expired`): create a new one

patch.description: Renames a session; it is a heartbeat too. Other clients see the new name from then on: the devices the session is a member of send `device_state` (`cause: access`). `401` once it has ended.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The secret session id

401.description: Unknown or expired session

post.description: Keeps a session alive. `401` once it has ended: create a new one.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The secret session id

401.description: Unknown or expired session

oneOf.description: `400`: a lease route without a session.
`403`: a write on a `ro-shared` device by a session that doesn't own it.

`409`: changing to `exclusive` while other sessions are members or other clients hold the
camera, without `force`.
Another client's live capture or burst.

`423`: above meta on an `exclusive` device (or anonymous on `ro-shared`), or taking a
lease another session owns, without `force`.

AccessError.description: A refused request. Rendered as `application/json`, `{"error": …}` plus context.

AccessState.description: Who may use the device and who does.

members.description: The sessions that connected to or used the device, in the order they joined.

oneOf.description: The session holding the device's lease; `null` on a `shared` device.

ApiError.description:
The JSON body of the refusals that came with sessions (`400`, `401`). Existing errors keep
their `500 text/plain` bodies.

link_mtu.description: MTU of the local interface the camera is reached over; the search doesn't go above it.

packet_size.description: The packet size now set: the largest that reached this host.

previous.description: The packet size before the search.

test_packets.description:
Whether the camera answered test packets at all. When it doesn't, nothing could be
measured and `packet_size` equals `previous`.

bit_depth.description:
Significant bits per pixel. Above 8, raw images are little-endian `u16`s. `null` until the
first frame.

error.description: Why the job failed. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.

expires_at.description: When the finished job will be dropped from the server. `null` until it finishes.

failed_count.description: Frames attempted and failed so far; non-zero only with `on_failure = skip`.

height.description: Frame height. `null` until the first frame is captured.

pixel_format.description: The `PixelFormat` the camera actually streamed in. `null` until the first frame.

width.description: Frame width. `null` until the first frame is captured; every frame of a job shares it.

client_id.description: The session that started it; `null` for an anonymous one.

ClientRef.description: A client as the others see it. `by` in events, the members of a device.

CloseReason.description:
Why a device was closed. Carried by the slot's stop signal, so a capture loop that ends because
of it can tell its client why.

access.description: Who may use the device and who does, as the asking client sees it.

ConnectedDevice.description: An entry of `GET /devices/connected`: the device and its access state.

CreateSessionRequest.description: `POST /sessions`. Both fields are optional, and so is the body.

name.description: Shown to other clients, e.g. `webapp · Firefox` or `line-script`.

timeout_s.description:
Seconds without a heartbeat before the session ends. Defaults to the server's
`--session-timeout` and is clamped to 5..=600.

DeviceAccess.description:
`GET /devices/{id}/access`: who may use the device and who does, and what the asking client
may do.

oneOf.description: The running live capture or burst, or `null`.

members.description: The sessions that connected to or used the device, in the order they joined.

oneOf.description: The session holding the lease; `null` on a `shared` device.

DeviceState.description: Everything about a device another client may want to show.

oneOf.description: The running burst job, or `null`.
The running live capture, or `null`.

closed.description: Whether the device is closed after this request (also `true` if it wasn't connected).

members.description: The sessions still members of the device.

seq.description: Global and increasing. Clients use it only to notice gaps.

Event.description: One message on the events socket: `{"seq":118,"time":"…","type":"feature_changed",…}`.

oneOf.description:
The first message on a socket: who you are and every connected device. Its `seq` is the
last one the snapshot includes.
Who made the change; `null` for anonymous clients and the server itself.
Why a device was closed; `null` for every other cause.

allOf.description: A device's complete state, after it changed.

oneOf.description: A device's complete state, after it changed.

A feature was written. It carries no value, since a write changes dependent features too:
read again what you display.
A command feature was executed.

A client lost its lease, its membership or its live capture or burst to another session's
forced lease.
A session ended.
This socket fell behind and lost events: read the state again.

FeatureState.description: A feature's live state: its value plus what a UI needs to offer it right now.

available.description:
The device's `pIsImplemented`/`pIsAvailable` conditions hold. An unavailable feature
(e.g. a frame rate in a line-scan mode) can be neither read nor written.

available_entries.description:
For an enum: the integer values of the entries the device currently offers. An entry
listed in `/gc/categories` but missing here is not supported right now.

error.description: Why this feature's state is incomplete, e.g. `Feature not found` or a failed read.

locked.description: A `pIsLocked` condition holds: the feature can be read but not written now.

min.description: Evaluated bounds of an `Integer`/`Float` feature, when the device declares them.

oneOf.description: `null` when the feature isn't known (see `error`).

value.description:
Same format as `GET /gc/feature/{name}`. `null` for a command, a write-only feature, an
unavailable one, or when the read failed (see `error`).

names.description: Feature names, as listed by `/gc/categories`. 1 to 256 of them.

selected.description:
For a selector (e.g. `GainSelector`): the features whose value depends on it, from the
node's `<pSelected>` elements. Empty for every other feature.

HolderKind.description: What holds a device's camera for a long time.

HolderRef.description: The holder of a device, as others see it.

client_id.description: The session that started it; `null` for an anonymous client.

OnFailure.description: What to do when a frame in the middle of a burst cannot be captured.

PacketSizeInfo.description: A camera's stream packet size, what it may be set to, and the link it travels over.

inc.description: Packet sizes are multiples of this.

link_mtu.description:
MTU of the local interface the camera is reached over. A larger packet size never
arrives. `null` when it can't be determined (only Linux hosts report it).

local_ip.description: This host's address on that interface.

min.description: Smallest and largest allowed packet size, both multiples of `inc`.

packet_size.description:
`GevSCPSPacketSize`: the size of each stream packet as a whole IP datagram (IP and UDP
headers included), in bytes. Every grab, live stream and burst uses it as it is.

PixelDepth.description: The pixel depth a client asks for.

name.description: The new name other clients see; `null` or missing removes it.

Role.description: A client's role on a device, following from the mode and the lease.

client_id.description: Public: how other clients see this one (8 hex characters).

heartbeat_interval_s.description: How often to send a heartbeat: a third of the timeout.

session_id.description: Secret: send it as `X-Racs-Session` or `?session=` with every request of this client.

SessionInfo.description: An entry of `GET /sessions`. Never carries a `session_id`.

devices.description: The devices this session is a member of.

last_seen.description: The last heartbeat or request carrying the session, RFC 3339.

owns.description: The devices whose lease this session holds.

since.description: When the session was created, RFC 3339.

force.description: Take the lease from another session, or evict other clients for `exclusive`.

format.description:
`raw` (width*height pixels, 1 or 2 bytes each depending on `bit_depth`), `jpeg`, or `zstd`
(the same pixels losslessly compressed, decoded as described for the live stream).

max_failures.description: With `on_failure = skip`, how many failed frames to tolerate. Omit for unlimited.

oneOf.description: `abort` (default) or `skip`.
`mono8` (default) or `mono16`. See `BurstJobInfo.bit_depth` for what the camera granted.

quality.description:
JPEG quality 1-100, default 80. Ignored for `raw` and `zstd`, and clamped rather than
rejected.

StateCause.description: What a `device_state` event reports a change of.

StreamErrorInfo.description: What `GET /devices/{id}/stream/error` returns. All-null for a device that never streamed.

active_stream.description: Whether a live stream is currently attached to this device.

last_error.description: The last error from any live stream on this device, or `null` if there has not been one.

viewers.description: How many live-stream sockets are open on this device: the viewers of its capture.

StreamInfo.description: The opening text message of a live stream, repeated when the geometry changes.

bit_depth.description:
Significant bits per pixel. Above 8, raw frames carry two little-endian bytes per pixel
in the range `0..2^bit_depth`; JPEG frames always carry the top 8 of them.

format.description: `"jpeg"`, `"raw"` or `"zstd"` — the encoding of every binary message that follows.

packet_size.description:
`GevSCPSPacketSize` the stream runs with: bytes per GVSP packet, IP and UDP headers
included.

pixel_format.description: The pixel format the frames were acquired in, read back from the camera.

session.name: X-Racs-Session
session.description: A session id from `POST /sessions`. Optional: requests without one are anonymous. WebSockets send it as the query parameter `?session=` instead; a request carrying both with different values is refused with `400 session_conflict`.
